 33m ago GOAL! Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United (Palmer 64 pen) 
 34m ago RED CARD: Martinez (Manchester United) 
 36m ago Penalty for Chelsea! 
 47m ago GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United (Rogers 50)

 Lisandro Martínez gets the cold shoulder from Manchester United manager Michael Carrick after his red card. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters Scott Murray Sat 31 Oct 2026 10.28 EDT First published on Sat 31 Oct 2026 07.00 EDT Share Key events 24m ago VAR: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 26m ago GOAL! Chelsea 3-0 Manchester United (Estevao 71) 
 33m ago GOAL! Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United (Palmer 64 pen) 
 34m ago RED CARD: Martinez (Manchester United) 
 36m ago Penalty for Chelsea! 
 47m ago GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United (Rogers 50) 
 1h ago HALF TIME: Chelsea 0-0 Manchester United 
 1h ago VAR: Chelsea 0-0 Manchester United 
 1h ago GOAL! Chelsea 0-1 Manchester United (Cunha 34)

 3h ago Preamble 
 now 10.28 EDT 90 min +8: Chelsea stroke the ball around the back, running the clock down in drama-free fashion. They’ve earned the right in this second half.
 Share 41s ago 10.27 EDT 90 min +7: Palmer dances his way into the United box from the right. For a second, things look like opening up for him, but Heaven sticks to his shoulder and ushers the ball out for a goal kick. That’s Palmer’s last act of the afternoon, as he makes way for Quenda.
 Share 2m ago 10.25 EDT 90 min +6: The xG now reads Chelsea 2.11 to Manchester United’s 1.18.
 Share 3m ago 10.24 EDT 90 min +4: … so when you’re luck’s out, you’re luck’s out. Manchester United can’t catch a break. That would have been a hell of a goal, but Penders wasn’t having a bar of it! Meanwhile up the other end, Palmer blazes a good chance over. It could have been 2-1; it could have been 3-0.
 Share 4m ago 10.23 EDT 90 min +2: … and they’re inches away from getting one! The corner’s half cleared to Mbeumo, who shapes like prime-era Zinedine Zidane and absolutely larrups a rising drive towards the top-right corner! The ball caroms off the underside of the bar and out! A sensational shot … and a save to match, because Penders got a fingernail to that, diverting it onto the woodwork! Awesome play all round!
 Share 6m ago 10.22 EDT 90 min +1: Zirkzee chops his way past Colwill down the right and earns Manchester United a corner. A goal here would set the cat amongst the pigeons.
 Share 8m ago 10.20 EDT 90 min: There will be ten (!) additional minutes. Michael Carrick must wonder what he’s done to deserve this.
 Share 8m ago 10.19 EDT 89 min: Mount, formerly of Chelsea , clatters into Palmer and probably should go into the book, but the referee shows mercy. Incidentally, Zirkzee picked up a yellow a couple of minutes ago, for another poor challenge. United have unravelled spectacularly, yet arguably not that predictably, in this second half.
 Share 10m ago 10.17 EDT 87 min: A triple change for Chelsea . Gusto, Welbeck and Barco come on for Neto, Caicedo and Estevao, who deserved a goal today, but won’t be getting one.
 Share Updated at  10.17 EDT 12m ago 10.15 EDT 85 min: Estevao jinks in from the right, one-twos with Palmer, and whips a glorious low curler towards the bottom left. Lammens saves excellently. Estevao must wonder how he’s not on the scoresheet.
 Share 14m ago 10.14 EDT 84 min: Zirkzee has a speculative dig from distance. It’s something, better than nothing, but easy for Penders. Chelsea go up the other end and Estevao’s shot deflects into the path of Lammens. “I’m sure Martinez wants out of this,” writes Tim Stappard. “I wish the rest of them wanted out too.”
 Share 15m ago 10.13 EDT 83 min: Hats off to Manchester United’s travelling support. They’re chanting their love for this famous old club, loud and long, despite the nonsense unfolding in front of them.
 Share 16m ago 10.12 EDT 81 min: Mbeumo is booked for delaying the restart as Palmer tries to take a quick free kick. “What was Carrick scribbling away frantically just then?” wonders Andrew Goudie. “His resignation letter?” You could hardly blame him, given the performance of his senior defenders in this second half.
 Share 17m ago 10.10 EDT 80 min: … Zirkzee should clear, but takes a poor touch and gifts Palmer possession. Palmer aims for the top left, but gets the shot all wrong. “If Zirkzee is the answer, what is the question?” asks rhetoric’s Joe Johnson. “Nothing good, I fear.”
 Share 18m ago 10.09 EDT 79 min: Palmer wanders past Maguire down the left, way too easily. He crosses for Estevao, who really wants a goal having had two disallowed. He shoots. Deflected. Corner. From which …
 Share 19m ago 10.08 EDT 78 min: On TNT, Joe Cole suggests that Martinez is “at the scene of the crime too often” and his United career has run its course. It’s hard to disagree.
 Share 21m ago 10.07 EDT 77 min: Diallo can’t continue. Zirkzee comes on in his stead. “Is it just me or everyone who thinks Martinez is pulling a ‘Romero move’ from last season?” wonders Karen Asad. “It sure looks thay way and a move to Atleti beckons!”
 Share 22m ago 10.06 EDT 76 min: Diallo goes down feeling his leg. As he gets medical attention, Michael Carrick gives his captain Bruno Fernandes some tactical instruction. The horse already bolted.
 Share 23m ago 10.04 EDT 74 min: Estevao has had two goals chalked off for offside now. That one was much closer than the other. Meanwhile Chavarria comes on for Palestra.
 Share 24m ago 10.03 EDT VAR: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United
 That looked onside … but the naked eye can deceive. Estevao’s shoulder just off. Maguire, in the middle, getting away with one.
 Share 26m ago 10.02 EDT GOAL! Chelsea 3-0 Manchester United (Estevao 71)
 This is too easy. Way too easy. Lavia snaffles possession from Fernandes’s loose pass and lays off to Palmer, 30 yards out. He feeds Estevao down the inside-right channel. Estevao lashes a rising shot through and past Lammens, and into the top-right corner.
 Share 28m ago 10.00 EDT 70 min: Palmer spins around Mainoo. So easy. Mainoo clips him, and goes into the book. Manchester United are being given the runaround now, and are losing their collective composure.
 Share 29m ago 09.58 EDT 69 min: The resulting corner is cut back for Acheampong, whose low drive is fielded by Lammens. Everyone in Chelsea blue fancies a bit of this now.
 Share 30m ago 09.58 EDT 68 min: Estevao finds space down the right and rolls across for Palmer, who would be tapping home at the far stick had Maguire not extended a leg to poke around the post. What fine last-ditch defence.
 Share 31m ago 09.57 EDT 67 min: Some admin, as Maguire is booked for a late clip on Rogers, while Mount and Heaven come on for Cunha and Santos.
 Share 31m ago 09.56 EDT 65 min: “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” trill the Chelsea fans. But can you blame Michael Carrick for such idiocy? “What an absolute idiot Martinez is,” writes Joshua Keeling. “Feel so sorry for Carrick. We played so well in the first half, missed a hatful of chances, terrible defending to give away the first goal, and then Martinez does something as stupid as that. We should have been two or three up at half time, and now look. It’s disgraceful from the players. Not Carrick. The players.”
 Share 33m ago 09.54 EDT GOAL! Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United (Palmer 64 pen)
 Palmer’s spot kick is no good. Towards the bottom right, but not well hit. Lammens gets a big hand on it, and should stop it … but lets his hand flap back and allows the ball into the corner.
 View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Cole Palmer steps up … Photograph: David Klein/Reuters View image in fullscreen The ball squeezes past Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Chelsea’s lead is doubled.
 Photograph: David Cliff/EPA View image in fullscreen It never rains but it pours. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.13 EDT 34m ago 09.53 EDT RED CARD: Martinez (Manchester United)
 63 min: … a second yellow for Martinez. What an idiotic challenge, one minute and 22 seconds after his first yellow. As Martinez stomps down the tunnel, poor Michael Carrick doesn’t bother looking at his player. You can’t blame him for showing such clear disdain. All that big talk, and now this.
 Share 36m ago 09.52 EDT Penalty for Chelsea!
 62 min: VAR ushers the referee over to the screen. It’s surely going to be a penalty: Martinez brazenly barged into Fofana. And yes, the ref draws a TV screen in the air. A reckless challenge … a penalty … and …
 Share 37m ago 09.51 EDT 61 min: Yep, VAR is going to take a look.
 Share 37m ago 09.50 EDT 60 min: Estevao curls the resulting free kick into the mixer, forcing Maguire to head behind. Estevao sends the corner long. Fofana rises at the far stick. Martinez, not looking at the ball but facing his man, barges into Fofana. No penalty … but should it be a penalty? It should be a penalty.
 View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez, what are you doing? Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.01 EDT 38m ago 09.49 EDT 59 min: Rogers ballet-dances his way down the right, a couple of pirouettes sending Martinez into a literal flat spin. Martinez eventually hauls him down and earns himself a booking.
 Share 40m ago 09.48 EDT 58 min: United make the first change of the afternoon, replacing Baleba, who surely won’t be happy with his role in Chelsea’s goal, with Mainoo.
 Share 41m ago 09.46 EDT 56 min: Estevao tries to chop his way past Dalot down the right, but has to settle for a corner. Estevao takes it himself, and nearly scores directly, but Lammens handles well on his line.
 Share 43m ago 09.44 EDT 55 min: That was one hell of a goal from Chelsea’s perspective. Lavia broke up United’s attack and started one for Chelsea with a couple of shoogles of his hips. And Rogers’ run, wow. But United’s defence opened up egregiously. Maguire and Martinez not covering themselves in glory.
 Share Updated at  09.45 EDT 44m ago 09.43 EDT 53 min: A free kick for United out on the left. Fernandes swings a dangerous low ball to the far post, where Cunha inexplicably fails to connect. Anything on that, and it was an equaliser. Fernandes can’t believe he doesn’t have another assist to his long career list.
 Share 46m ago 09.41 EDT 51 min: Chelsea’s tails are up, and Estevao slides down the right before standing one up for Neto, whose looping header towards the top left is plucked from the sky by Lammens.
 Share 47m ago 09.40 EDT GOAL! Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United (Rogers 50)
 Lavia snaffles the ball in the centre circle, seeing off Mbeumo and Baleba in one movement, and flicks the ball to Rogers, who does the rest. Rogers sashays down the inside-left channel at pace, gliding past Maguire with disdain, entering the box, drawing Lammens, and dinking gently over the keeper and in. That’s an outrageous run and finish. Hats off to Lavia too!
 View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers dinks the ball past Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens to put Chelsea ahead. Photograph: Ian Walton/AP View image in fullscreen Rogers celebrates with Estevao. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters Share Updated at  09.50 EDT 50m ago 09.38 EDT 48 min: United’s xG has risen to 1.09. Given absolutely nothing’s happened since the start of the second half, you do have to wonder sometimes.
 Share 51m ago 09.37 EDT 47 min: A slow start to the second half, so Stamford Bridge breaks into song in the hope of getting the home heroes going. “That was surely a first half where both teams needed Danny Welbeck as striker,” quips Rick Harris. “Can’t understand why United let him go.”
 Share 53m ago 09.35 EDT Chelsea get the second half started. The hosts will be looking for improvement, because Manchester United had the upper hand during that first period: to illustrate, Michael Carrick’s men won the xG battle by 0.28 to 1.01. But there are no half-time changes.
 Share 54m ago 09.33 EDT TNT have a quick chat with Michael Carrick before the restart. “We’ve played really well … done a lot of good things … we want to make that count … the game’s always in the balance here … we need to take our opportunities … we need a big second half.”
 Share 1h ago 09.29 EDT … and also allow us to introduce our new satire segment, That Was Half Time That Was. “Afternoon Scott,” begins Stephen Carr. “I’d like to take this opportunity to say that Aston Villa are a massive club with incredible heritage and are dead clever and get all the girls.”
 Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for ‘unacceptable insults’ Read more Topical calypsos to follow.
 Share 1h ago 09.22 EDT I mean … both teams have had a goal ruled out for offside. Both attacks look lively; both defences are a risible shambles. It’s been great fun! We just need a goal. We’re still going to get one or two or five, right? Anyway, here’s the half-time postbag …
 “I agree with you, there should be goals in this game, especially given that both defenses are holier than a very tattered shroud of Turin. But conversely, every attacker seems cursed by all the gods of every pantheon. It feels like that if a breakthrough comes it will be an absurd own goal” – Kári Tulinius
 “Fans saying that the whole Fernandes (and Martinez) saga wouldn’t have happened under Ferguson need to realise how different the footballing landscape is now. Ferguson was the manager, not the coach, to paraphrase Ruben Amorim. He had full control and final say over everything. If he was in charge today, he would have to answer to the sporting director/director of football etc just like every other coach has to. He would also be subject to the same barrage of abuse that Carrick no doubt has been this week from the respective players agents. Football ‘managers’ have their hands tied behind their back these says; they’re not really in charge of anything - see also Arne Slot and Mo Salah last season” – Dave Estherby
 “I know Michael Carrick needs all the help he can get, but having Bruno Fernandes’s brother running the line seems a bit much” – Gary Naylor
 Share 1h ago 09.18 EDT HALF TIME: Chelsea 0-0 Manchester United
 It’s been fast. It’s been fun. The defences are all over the shop. Goals are surely just a matter of time. Surely? 
 Share 1h ago 09.17 EDT 45 min: Estevao barges his way down the right and shoots straight at Lammens from a tight angle. He had Rogers clear in the middle. Seconds earlier, Mbeumo nearly got through on goal down the United left. Has a basketball game ever ended 0-0?
 Share 1h ago 09.15 EDT 43 min: … and now, up the other end, Neto spins Maguire down the left and drags a shot across the face of goal when one-on-one with Lammens. How on earth is this still 0-0?!
 Share 1h ago 09.15 EDT 42 min: Diallo spins the hapless Fofana down the right and he’s clear! He enters the box, opens his body, and aims a curler towards the top left. Just over. A big miss, though to be fair to Fofana, he got back and nibbled at Diallo to put him off.
 Share 1h ago 09.14 EDT 41 min: … so having said that, Estevao probes down the right and wins Chelsea a corner. It’s swung towards the near post. The ball clanks off Palestra in slow motion, then off Caicedo, and finally off the right-hand post and away! But it wouldn’t have counted, because the ball hit Caicedo’s arm. All in super slo-mo.
 Share 1h ago 09.12 EDT 40 min: Chelsea are struggling to string anything together, and their fans are beginning to get a bit agitated.
 Share 1h ago 09.10 EDT 39 min: A corner from the right leads to another from the left. Fernandes loops it in. Colwill wins a header and Penders claims the dropping ball. Chelsea needed that. United have enjoyed 71 percent of possession in the last five minutes.
 Share 1h ago 09.09 EDT 38 min: Diallo jinks into the Chelsea box from the right and aims for the bottom left. His shot is deflected behind for another Manchester United corner. Chelsea are clinging on at the moment.
 Share 1h ago 09.08 EDT 36 min: The lead wouldn’t have flattered Manchester United . They’ve been extremely lively in attack; they’ve been the better team. “Has Dr Tottenham retired and handed their practice over to Chelsea?” wonders Sean Orlowicz.
 Share 1h ago 09.07 EDT VAR: Chelsea 0-0 Manchester United
 … and it’s just as easily chalked off. Cunha had been nudged into an offside position as Maguire was winning his header. The blood drains from Michael Carrick’s face. When your luck’s out …
 Share 1h ago 09.06 EDT GOAL! Chelsea 0-1 Manchester United (Cunha 34)
 Fernandes hits the corner long from the right. Maguire wins a header at the far post. Cunha stoops and guides a header into the bottom right from close range. Easy as that!
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United Matheus Cunha (centre) wheels away in celebration after finding the net. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at  09.18 EDT 1h ago 09.04 EDT 33 min: … and Fernandes’ corner from the right leads to another on the left. Fernandes trots across to take this one as well.
 Share 1h ago 09.04 EDT 32 min: Fofana, who didn’t have a good game at Anfield in the League Cup during the week, allows Diallo to rip the ball away from him on halfway. Diallo steams clear, and enters the box, shooting from an angle on the right. Penders kicks around the post, saving his defender’s blushes. For now …
